SHAP: year indicators ranked highest (London 2021 and 2025; Birmingham–WM 2024, 2022 and 2025). Among environmental predictors, NDBI led in London and built-up probability in Birmingham–WM. Higher NDBI and built-up probability raised predicted LST; higher NDVI and elevation lowered it. SHAP shows association, not cause.

About this dashboard

Data and method

Landsat 8/9 Collection 2 Level 2 imagery within the heatwave windows was processed in Google Earth Engine to derive LST and environmental drivers: NDVI, MNDWI, NDBI, built-up probability, MODIS albedo and SRTM elevation. Mean heatwave LST was aggregated to 2021 MSOAs. Extreme-heat MSOAs are at or above each city's own 90th percentile (London 38.6 °C, Birmingham–WM 37.2 °C). Population, residents aged 65+ and deprived households are from ONS 2021 data. HadUK-Grid 1 km air temperature (2021–2024) gives independent context. At pixel level, London's median LST (36.43 °C) was higher than Birmingham–WM's (34.21 °C).

Read with care

P90 classes show relative surface-heat hazard within each city, not a shared absolute threshold. Demographic counts show potential residential exposure, not personal exposure or health outcomes. Absolute totals differ partly because Greater London has far more MSOAs and residents.
